headline: Dry high pressure holds: mild, sunny Bluegrass afternoons continue while the Upstate stays cooler and breezy before a Monday warm-up
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Sunny, rain-free weather continues across Danville and the Bluegrass through Monday beneath persistent surface high pressure and a dry midlevel ridge. Afternoon temperatures remain near 70 while clear nights favor localized river-valley fog and patchy frost in the coldest sheltered spots.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 8:15 AM EDT, KDVK was clear at 36°F with a 36°F dew point and calm wind. At 7:54 AM, KLEX was clear at 38°F with a 37°F dew point and calm wind; visibility was 8 miles. No precipitation or official NWS alert was present at issuance.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Danville point. Independent concern is limited to localized river-valley fog and patchy frost late tonight into early Sunday; a widespread freeze is not expected.
days.forecast: Full sunshine follows the chilly start as surface high pressure and a dry midlevel ridge suppress clouds and rain. Danville's most likely high is 70°F with light and variable wind. Tonight turns clear and chilly; the most likely Danville low is near 41°F, while sheltered valleys may reach the upper 30s with localized fog or frost toward Sunday dawn.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Sunday at issuance. Independent concern is limited to patchy river-valley fog late Sunday night into Monday morning; isolated frost is possible in the coldest sheltered spots.
days.forecast: Any localized valley fog dissipates quickly, followed by sunshine and a light east wind. Danville's most likely high is 71°F. Sunday night stays clear with a most likely low near 42°F; colder sheltered valleys may fall into the upper 30s with patchy fog toward Monday dawn.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Monday at issuance. A single colder NAM profile supports localized valley fog or frost late Monday night, but a widespread dense-fog or freeze event is not expected.
days.forecast: Sunny and mild beneath persistent high pressure, with a most likely Danville high of 71°F and light southwest or variable wind. Monday night is mostly clear to partly cloudy with a most likely low near 43°F. The NAM's colder, foggier solution is not corroborated by full-period GFS, GEFS or ECMWF guidance, so only localized valley fog or frost is retained toward Tuesday dawn.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays rain-free through Monday. Most likely Danville highs are 70°F, 71°F and 71°F, with most likely nighttime lows of 41°F, 42°F and 43°F. Localized pre-dawn river-valley fog or frost remains possible, but no widespread freeze or official alert is expected.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather and daytime temperatures; moderate on exact sheltered-valley lows and localized fog or frost placement

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: The Clemson–Central corridor remains dry through Monday. A shallow, mostly sunny cold-air-damming wedge keeps the weekend cooler and breezy with northeast gusts below advisory criteria, then the wedge begins to erode Monday as winds ease and temperatures rebound.
upstate.currentConditions: At 8:05 AM EDT, KCEU was 53°F with a 47°F dew point, a northeast wind near 7 mph and an overcast deck near 3,000 feet. At 8:15 AM, KLQK was near 55°F with a 48°F dew point, a northeast wind near 8 mph and an overcast deck near 3,000 feet. Visibility remained at least 10 miles, so the shallow cloud deck was not classified as fog. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Clemson point. Independent concern is limited to breezy northeast flow with gusts around 16–25 mph, remaining below advisory and verification-hazard thresholds. No corridor frost or freeze is expected.
days.forecast: Localized shallow stratus near Pickens clears around 10–11 AM, followed by sunshine beneath a dry cold-air-damming wedge. Clemson's most likely high is 67°F. Northeast wind runs 7–12 mph with gusts near 16–25 mph. Tonight is mostly clear with a most likely Clemson low near 46°F; sheltered Central and Pickens County locations may reach 38–40°F.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Sunday at issuance. Breezy northeast flow remains an independent concern, with gusts around 18–26 mph but below advisory and verification-hazard thresholds.
days.forecast: There is a 15–25% chance of localized shallow stratus around daybreak, followed by sunshine and a persistent dry wedge. Clemson's most likely high is 68°F. Northeast wind runs 7–13 mph with gusts near 18–26 mph. Sunday night is clear with a most likely Clemson low near 45°F and sheltered Central or Pickens County locations around 38–40°F.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Monday at issuance, and no significant independent hazard is expected. The weekend wedge weakens, with lighter wind and no corridor freeze expected.
days.forecast: The dry wedge begins to weaken, allowing a sunnier, warmer afternoon with a most likely Clemson high near 71°F. Northeast wind eases to 2–7 mph with gusts around 8–17 mph. Monday night remains mostly clear with a most likely Clemson low near 45°F; sheltered Central and Pickens County locations may reach 37–39°F.

upstate.bottomLine: The Clemson–Central corridor remains dry. Most likely Clemson highs are 67°F, 68°F and 71°F, with most likely lows of 46°F, 45°F and 45°F; sheltered Central and Pickens County locations fall into the upper 30s. Northeast gusts of 16–26 mph continue through Sunday before easing Monday. No official alert is active.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather; moderate-high on weekend temperatures and wind, and moderate on Monday's warming because GFS is warmer than ECMWF and NAM guidance

sourceNotes: No official NWS alert was active for the Danville or Clemson point at the 12:01:35Z checks. Official alerts remain separate from this independent analysis.

The 10:56Z Louisville and 10:58Z Greenville-Spartanburg discussions, official point forecasts, HRRR 06Z/10Z, RAP 09Z, NAM and NAM 3-km 06Z, GFS and GEFS 06Z, and the refreshed official ECMWF 06Z extraction agree on a dry 72-hour period. Monday Upstate guidance spans roughly 67.5–74.6°F; the calibrated 68–74°F public range remains centered on the 71°F most-likely value, while reduced confidence and the documented benchmarks preserve the cross-model uncertainty.

Current KLEX and KGSP-area BUFKIT profiles were consulted for temperature, inversion, fog and northeast-wind structure. BUFKIT was used as a visualization interface for underlying model cycles and was not counted as a separate model.

The validated initial seven-model GRIB package was generated at 12:16:21Z with all seven requested models present; HRRR, RAP and NAM 3-km have normal partial horizons. Its older 00Z ECMWF member was superseded for the final synthesis by a fresh official 06Z extraction: the validated Danville summary was generated at 12:45:31Z, direct Clemson-area point records were generated at 12:50:13Z, and the extracted records extend through 15Z October 27, beyond this candidate's full horizon.

Contains modified ECMWF Open Data, selected and processed locally for independent forecast research under CC BY 4.0. The fresh 06Z point fields were manually reviewed and were not copied automatically into the public forecast.
College of DuPage radar showed no coherent precipitation near either region, while satellite imagery showed only shallow localized cloud near the Blue Ridge and no organized deep cloud shield.
Chris Bailey's October 24 Kentucky Weather Center post describes the dry, stubborn pattern continuing until around Halloween weekend; that possible change is outside this 72-hour forecast.

The latest cumulative accuracy summary was consulted: 28 verified forecast IDs, 74 verified checkpoints and 75.1% all-category accuracy. Updated station corrections, empirical range widths, regime-specific model weights, fog timing and official-alert handling were applied.

Temperature cards retain calibrated regional coverage ranges, while prose supplies narrower most-likely Danville and Clemson values. Wider nighttime ranges account for terrain-driven station differences rather than uncertainty at one exact point.

Localized Upstate low stratus was kept separate from fog because reported visibility remained 10 miles. Weekend breezes remain below the 25 mph sustained and 35 mph gust verification-hazard thresholds, so no threshold wind event window was issued.
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
